thread:
deploy-bot: ALERT: proposing temporary SDK client pin for sdk-js on hosted clients to v3.5.2 for a 3h window (01:30-04:30 UTC) due to auth signature mismatch observed in canary after sdk v3.6 rollout. Affects: token-signed requests from older runtimes. Linking ticket INF-4891. Tagging @eng-platform and @security.

maya: Noted. Brief summary of the failure mode? need to explain to customers if we pin.

liam: Canary failure: some clients sending signed headers using sha1 instead of sha256 after transpile change in v3.6. Canary id: canary-sdk-20260323-7. Error seen: 401 with "invalid_signature" about 2.7% of requests at 95th percentile.

clare: So this is a client-side regression. Is immediate pin feasible without a deploy? We can toggle the CDN routing to a compatibility shim but that takes longer. Pinging will keep gateway accepting old signatures for the window. Ops, can you enforce the compatibility header?

infra-bot: Note: compatibility-accept-sha1 feature is toggleable via featureflag service (ff/accept-legacy-signature). We can enable for the hold window. If enabled, telemetry will mark requests with header X-SIG-VERSION=legacy.

maya: Preference: avoid breaking customers. Enable ff/accept-legacy-signature for 3h, publish advisory, then revoke the feature after fix rollout. Also start a coordinated downstream SDK hotfix (v3.6.1) with the transpile fix.

liam: Timeline check: we can cut v3.6.1 build in 90m, tests + canary 30m, then opt to unpin. If FF is enabled, please make sure we add telemetry to count legacy-signature hits so we know scope.

clare: Can we auto-reject legacy if error-rate increases >0.5% or latency regressions show up? We should avoid exposing more surface area.

maya: Agreed. Proposed control logic: 1) enable ff for a 3h window 2) monitor legacy-signature rate and 401 volume 3) if legacy-signature rate >5% sustained for 10m, notify customer-ops and schedule support banner 4) if other regressions (latency/error) flip ff off and rollback to previous gateway behavior.

infra-bot: Actionable steps: 
- enable ff: POST /ff/toggles/accept-legacy-signature {"enabled":true, "expires":"2026-03-23T04:30:00Z"}
- add telemetry filter: /telemetry/filters add legacy_sig_tag
- mark release note draft: /release-notes/drafts/INF-4891

liam: I'll cut v3.6.1 PR and request a quick security review (signature lib touched). target canary in 2h.

maya: I'll own customer comms. Draft advisory: "Temporary compatibility flag enabled to accept legacy sha1 signatures after sdk-js v3.6; we will release sdk-js v3.6.1 with fix and advise upgrading."

clare: Ops-note for rollback: if enabling ff causes >1% increase in 5xx for gateway over baseline for 5m, infra-bot will auto-disable flag and post in this thread. Also tag @eng-oncall.

infra-bot: FF enabled at 01:32 UTC. Legacy-sig traffic initially 0.3% of total. Telemetry tags live: https://telemetry.internal/streams/legacy-sig?c=canary-sdk-20260323-7

liam: PR opened: github.com/redwood/sdk-js/pull/2104 includes the transpile fix. CI green. Canary started.

maya: Posted customer advisory draft in #customer-success and linked release-notes draft.

infra-bot: Canary metrics (01:50 UTC): legacy-sig=1.9% (spike during beta), 401-rate due to invalid_signature=0.9% (reduced since ff enabled), gateway 5xx unchanged. No latency regressions.

clare: Good. Proceed with build and staged release of v3.6.1. Plan timeline: canary -> regional rollout -> unflag after 24h. If canary shows >2% 401 after fix, rollback plan is to re-enable ff and pause rollout.

deploy-bot: Scheduling staged release of sdk-js v3.6.1 canary in 30m. Will post updates.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll publish advisory at 02:15 UTC and coordinate support.

infra-bot: FF auto-expiry set to 04:30 UTC. Will auto-disable unless extended.

deploy-bot: Canary completed: v3.6.1 shows 401 down to 0.05% and legacy-sig usage decreased as clients upgraded. Flag toggled off at 04:29 UTC. Closing ticket INF-4891; follow-up: remind partners to upgrade and include note in next weekly changelog.
